pr_title: statistics, sessionctx: introduce topn assisted cardinality estimation for string matching functions
pr_body:
### What problem does this PR solve?


Issue Number: close #36209

### What is changed and how it works?

- Provide the method to estimate the selectivity of an expression by evaluating the TopN and NULL in the stats.
- Provide a variable to control the default selectivity of like and regexp.
- Modify the code structure of `Selectivity()` to fit the new logic.

issue_context.title: Add an option to enhance cardinality estimation of like/regexp using the TopN in stats
issue_context.body:
## Background
Currently, we meet some cases where the cardinality estimation of string matching functions (like and regexp) is bad. When the pattern is complex, we are unable to build the function into `Range`s to estimate it with higher precision.

## Enhancement
To mitigate this, we can use the statistics to estimate selectivity. Specifically, we can (1) evaluate the expressions with values in the TopN, and (2) consider the NULL count by evaluating the expressions with NULL.
Currently, for convenience and due to the limitation of current statistics, we only apply this optimization on expressions that only involve one column, only when this column is not a non-binary collation string column, and statistics on this column (or a single column index on this column) is available and it's ver2,

And we can also provide a variable to control the default selectivity of the string matching functions.

Currently, we will make the default behavior unchanged, and the user can use the variable to control the feature.

review_comments: It seems this part is the same as the below. Can we move this out of the `if else` part.

No.
Because `Column` and `Index` are two different types. So the `stats` in the `if` and the `else` are different types.
What's the purpose for this operation? It seems the following part doesn't use the `col`.

You can see the comment of `Column.Index`. When execution, we don't use `UniqueID` anymore, we use `Index` to locate a column in the chunk.
Here, because the chunk only has one column, so we just set it to 0.
Please add this part to the comments.
Should the `selected` reset here like the `c`?
We don't need to. Because it will be reset in `VectorizedFilter`.
I updated and reset it anyway.
From the previous discussion, we want a smaller value in fact?

Yes.
But considering the risk of regression, we keep the default value unchanged. If there are scenarios that need this optimization or a smaller default value, the user needs to modify it manually.
Besides, please add more comments to explain why we should do this.
When will `Len(selected) != 1` happens? It seems the meaning here is some null values are considered. Some are not. Why not here just set `nullSel = 0`.

It's not expected to happen.
NULL has been considered in `VectorizedFilter`. If `len(selected) != 1`, it means this evaluation doesn't return one result, and that's not expected.
What about changing it to 0.1 when the set value is 0 together with a warning thrown out.

I prefer to keep it unchanged.
If we change it to 0.1 when setting it to 0, we won't be able to know whether it's a true 0.1 or if we actually set it to 0 afterward.
